headline: Circles are unique among shapes—no beginning, no end, infinite symmetry, the basis of wheels and orbits
universal_truth: Some shapes recur because they solve fundamental problems; nature repeats what works
fun_facts: Circles enclose the maximum area for a given perimeter—that's why soap bubbles are spherical
The wheel is one of humanity's most important inventions, but no animals evolved wheels
Pi (π) is the ratio of any circle's circumference to its diameter—the same for every circle ever
discussion_questions: Why do circles appear so often in nature?
What makes the wheel such a powerful invention?
What cycles in your life go around and around?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Circles are everywhere: the sun, the moon, pupils in eyes, tree rings, ripples in water. Unlike squares or triangles, circles have no corners, no start, no end. They're mathematically special and practically essential. What makes circles so universal?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Nature seems to love circles. Eyes are round. Planets are round. Water drops are round. Is this coincidence, or is there something fundamental about the circular shape?

options.text: Circles are efficient—they enclose maximum area with minimum perimeter and have perfect symmetry in all directions
options.response: Yes. Circles are mathematically optimal. Surface tension pulls drops into spheres. Gravity pulls planets into spheres. When forces are equal in all directions, circles emerge.

options.text: Circles look pleasing to the eye, so nature evolved toward them
options.response: Aesthetics might follow function—circles are common because they work, not because they look good...

q1.title: Optimal Efficiency
q1.script: Circles enclose the most area for a given perimeter. That's why cells are roughly spherical—maximum volume for minimum surface. Efficiency drives circular shapes in biology, physics, and engineering.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Optimal Efficiency"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Power of Wheels
q2.script: The wheel transformed civilization. Rolling eliminates friction that dragging creates. Circular motion converts to linear motion and back. Yet no animal evolved wheels—nature uses legs. Technology discovered what evolution missed.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Cycles and Repetition
q3.script: Circles symbolize cycles—seasons, life cycles, orbits. What goes around comes around. The circular shape suggests return, repetition, and eternity. No corner to stop at; the journey continues endlessly.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Some shapes recur because they solve fundamental problems. Circles teach that nature repeats what works. Look for patterns that appear across different domains—they're often optimal solutions.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 172. Tomorrow, we'll explore the strongest shape—triangles. Until then, notice circles around you—in nature, technology, and the cycles of your life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Circle Spotting - Find the Pattern
growTrack.learning_objective: Notice circular patterns in environment and life
growTrack.activity: Count circles today—in objects, in nature, in patterns of life. Why is each one circular? Notice which are physical (wheels, eyes) and which are conceptual (cycles, routines). Circles reveal optimization and repetition.
